label: GO after unrewarded a1->S2 rare; larger after prior unrewarded/S2 trial and S1-leaning belief
terms: (phase == GO) * last_is("a1 S2 u") ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a1 S2 u") * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a1 S2 u") * (tv("state", -2) == 2) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a1 S2 u") * np.clip(belief_lo, 0, 4)
explanation: Fires only at GO, and almost only when the previous trial was a1 -> S2 (rare) unrewarded (GO residual +0.52 there vs about -0.05 for every other previous-trial pattern; D1 and D2 are essentially zero). How large it gets within that case depends on observed history: bigger when the trial before was also unrewarded (w +0.24), bigger when the trial before also reached S2 (w +0.17), and it grows with the ideal observer belief that S1 is good (clipped log-odds, w +0.13 per unit). The a1 S2 u indicator alone gives dev R^2 0.45 beyond timing. With the 4 observed-only terms: dev 0.49, test 0.47, against an all-cue ceiling of 0.50 (all observed 0.49), so using observed quantities only costs little. Adding the future upcoming choice (action == 1) did not help (0.45 vs 0.45 for the indicator alone). Some fires are still under-predicted (actual about 1.3 vs predicted about 0.5 for some a1 S2 u GO steps), and some at the first trial of the window, where the previous trial is unknown, are missed.

issues: The 'trial before also reached S2 (+0.17)' claim is misleading as an additive effect. When the trial before is broken into its four state x reward patterns (inside GO after a1 S2 u, no belief term), the weights are: S1 rewarded +0.43, S1 unrewarded +0.46, S2 rewarded -0.04, S2 unrewarded +0.93, unknown +0.55. Reaching S2 only raises the feature when that trial was also unrewarded. An S2-rewarded trial before suppresses it to about 0, which the claimed terms predict as a boost. Adding the S2-and-unrewarded conjunction to the claimed terms flips the S2 weight to -0.47 and gives the conjunction +0.86.

The a1 S2 u indicator on its own gets a fitted weight of only +0.027 in the claimed model. So the 'GO residual +0.52' firing depends almost entirely on the modifiers (trial before unrewarded or S2, or belief favouring S1) and is not a uniform base response. The magnitude is close to binary (about 1.3 or about 0), and the additive modifiers only roughly capture this.

There is a systematic, recoverable miss class: GO on the window's first trial (prev_action == -1). There the feature reaches about 1.3 (misses show 1.34 / 1.32 / 1.38 / 1.19 against predictions of about 0.05). The agent's belief is still observable on that trial. Adding (phase == GO) * (prev_action == -1) * (prev_reward == 0) * clip(belief_lo, 0, 4) raises test R^2 from 0.470 to 0.523 (dev 0.554). This beats the stated 'all observed' ceiling of 0.49, so the ceiling understates what observed cues can reach.

With a 4-way table of the trial before plus belief plus the first-trial term (7 terms), test R^2 beyond timing is 0.537 against the claimed 0.470. That gap of about 0.07 comes from structure the label gets wrong or leaves out.
Minor: conditioning on this trial's choice being a1 (stay, a future variable) barely helps (test 0.472). The claim that the future choice does not help is consistent with this.
